notes:
Account background: Aegis builds a conversational front-end for mortgage and lending support; highly regulated, must retain audit logs and support data residency. They've built an internal vector DB and use embeddings + reranking + chat for customer-facing agents. Primary ask: committed Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput and lower unit cost vs hosted API. Also evaluating Private (VPC) because of residency/KMS requirements.

Key technical requirements (from discovery):
- Workloads: mixed (support chat ~70% reads with streaming responses, reranking ~20%, periodic bulk embeddings jobs ~10%)
- Latency target: 95th <= 150ms for short-chat turn (<=256 tokens); tail protection needed for peak concurrency
- Throughput target: sustained 200 qps for chat endpoints during peak 3-hour window; burst to 800 qps supported via autoscale/burst pool
- Context lengths: typical 1k tokens, occasionally 8k for escalations
- Acceptable fallbacks: degrade to smaller model variant or route to hosted for non-sensitive traffic

Cost-modeling work performed so far (deliverables and assumptions):
- Baseline POC: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (POC instance), measured raw token/sec ~95k tokens/sec aggregate with current model mix and batch settings; observed 40-55% effective GPU utilization after accounting for KV caching and I/O waits
- Scenario modeling: created 3 commit tiers for finance:
  Scenario A (Conservative): 4 reserved GPUs, assumed utilization 45% (avg), supports sustained 120 qps, estimated monthly tokens 1.6B. Estimated reserved-cost saving vs on-demand: ~18%. Unit economics: $0.000015/token (amortized infra + license) assuming Redwood dedicated pricing X and model runtime Y.
  Scenario B (Recommended): 8 reserved GPUs, assumed utilization 65% (avg) due to prefix caching and batching, supports sustained 320 qps with headroom. Estimated monthly tokens 4.0B. Estimated reserved-cost saving vs on-demand: ~38%. Unit economics: $0.000010/token. Break-even at ~52% utilization.
  Scenario C (Aggressive): 16 reserved GPUs, targeted utilization 70-75% for high committed discount, supports sustained 650 qps, monthly tokens ~8.2B. Unit economics: $0.000007/token, but requires multi-year commit to reach finance thresholds.
- Included hidden costs: cross-region egress estimates, KMS per-request costs, retention storage for audit logs. Modeled SLO credit exposure under 99.95% SLA and impact on finance reserve.
- Assumptions called out explicitly to finance: model mix stable, no major model size upgrades in first 12 months, KV cache hit-rate improvement to +20% with suggested prompt refactorization, tail-latency mitigation via two-tier routing.

SLA & negotiation points surfaced:
- Desired: 99.95% uptime for dedicated pool, latency SLO 95th <=150ms. Redwood default SLA language includes reasonable remediation; Legal wants explicit credit table for latency SLO misses and definition for 'service unit'.
- Need: clear escalation path, on-call rotas for incidents, and runbook for planned maintenance windows that impact capacity.

Recommended next actions (from AE + SE):
- Deliver final 3-year TCO spreadsheet comparing Scenario A/B/C vs on-demand with sensitivities (token growth + model upgrades).
- Provide KMS/HSM architecture diagram and SOC2 audit artifacts to security (linked in drive).
- Align on enterprise SLA addendum draft (legal + Redwood partnerships) and present to Aegis legal by 2024-12-20.
- Finance alignment call: walk through break-even analysis and utilization sensitivity (scheduled week of 2024-12-18).

Selling notes / risk profile:
- Upside: If Aegis accepts Scenario B, ARR is mid-six-figures and opens path for Private deployment across EU region.
- Risks: CFO requires 3-year cash-flow positive plan vs their current cloud spend; security still skeptical of external KMS unless HSM integration is explicit.

Stenographic call quotes: "If we can get unit cost to under $0.00001/token at scale we can justify committed spend" — VP Engineering.

Open items for Redwood team:
- Finalize per-token amortized unit cost including reserved GPU depreciation, SW license, infra ops (presented in spreadsheet tab 'unit-econ-v3').
- Confirm burst capacity SLA and pricing for overflow to hosted endpoints during peak (to avoid underprovisioning).
- Provide example A/B rollback plan for model upgrades affecting latency-based SLOs.

POC notes: caching improvements from SE reduced effective token load by ~28% on chat flows, which materially improves break-even for Scenario B. Recommend documenting prompt-level changes as part of onboarding playbook.
